get-channels.body:
`channelId` is an opaque UUID once it leaves this endpoint. Every downstream context that echoes it (sends, webhooks, logged transactions) drops the `(country, currency, channelType, rampType)` tuple, so integrators end up caching the lookup or re-fetching the full list just to render a label.

*Echo the denormalized tuple alongside `channelId`, or ship a stable composite key (e.g. `NG.bank.NGN.withdraw`) that survives in logs without a second API call.*

If a 🚧 warning callout is necessary to tell every integrator to drop `inactive` channels, the default should drop them too. Every careful integrator writes the same `.filter(c => c.status === "active")`; everyone who doesn't ships broken UIs.

*Default `GET /channels` to `status=active`; add `?status=all` as the explicit opt-in for admin-style callers.*

Widget integrators are told to filter by `widgetStatus` instead of `status` — the default-filter param should accept `widgetStatus=active` so widget callers stay on the same idiom.

More broadly: the response shape carries three near-parallel status fields (`status`, `widgetStatus`, `apiStatus`) with no doc-level guidance on how they can diverge. *Add a one-paragraph "which status do I read?" decision table.*

get-networks.body: Same shape as `Get Channels` — same callout, same case for server-side default filtering. *Default to `status=active`; add `?status=all` as the opt-in.*

No `GET /networks/{id}` endpoint exists, so resolving a `networkId` returned on a send (e.g. inside `destination.networkId`) to a human-readable bank name requires fetching the full country list and looking it up client-side.

*Add the by-ID endpoint, or include `networkName` on any response object that already carries a `networkId`.*

resolve-bank-account.body:
Two issues in one callout:

1. "Available in select countries" never enumerates which countries. Integrators discover the supported set by hitting 400s. *List supported ISO codes in the description, or expose `supportsBankResolution` on `Get Channels`.*
2. "Required for Nigeria" conflates endpoint scope with workflow. The endpoint validates a bank account; whether it's *required* before a send is a workflow decision. *Clarify whether `Submit Send Request` to NGN rejects sends that skipped this step.*

lookup-payment-by-sequenceid.body:
Two endpoints in the Sends group still use `/payments` paths while the rest are on `/send`:

- `Lookup Send by sequenceId` → `GET /payments/sequence-id/{id}` (this page)
- `Fail Send Pending Liquidity` → `POST /payments/{id}/fail-pending-liquidity`

Forces a `baseUrl + "/send"` helper to special-case two endpoints. *Ship `/send/...` aliases for the stragglers and deprecate `/payments/...` — or commit to keeping `/payments` everywhere. Pick one.*

submit-collection-request.body: Endpoint paths migrated to `/receive`, but the doc-site slugs and prose descriptions still use `collection` everywhere (`submit-collection-request`, `accept-collection-request`, "Accept a collection request for execution.", etc.). The Updated Terminology callout acknowledges the rename — the migration just isn't finished.

Error names (`CollectionNotFoundError`, `"Collection request expired"`) are probably back-compat on purpose — but the doc never says so. *Note the back-compat intent alongside this callout, and ship `ReceiveNotFoundError` as an alias so new integrators don't pick up the legacy name.*

create-webhook.anchor: Create a webhook for a given transaction state
create-webhook.body:
Request and response examples on this endpoint both use `"state": "collection.complete"`. The Webhooks / Events guides have moved to `RECEIVE.*` / `SEND.*` (e.g. `RECEIVE.COMPLETE`); the example here is stale.

*Update to `receive.complete`. Same check needed on `Update Webhook` and `List Webhooks`.*

The `state` field is described as "the transaction status event that this webhook will be activated for," but the description doesn't link to the canonical event list — integrators have to leave the page and hunt for it in the Events guide.

*Inline the list (or a link to it) in the body-parameter description.*

submit-settlement-request.body:
Two different services use the word "send" for two different operations, with no visual hint in the sidebar:

- Crypto Sends → `POST /business/send/crypto` (partner-rail disbursement, this endpoint).
- Custody → Create Send Transaction → `POST /custody/sends` (outbound from a custody wallet).

Base URLs differ (`/business` vs. `/custody`) but the sidebar doesn't surface that. *Prefix sidebar entries with the service name, or add a "Which API am I looking at?" intro that names the base URL.*

create-rfq.anchor: Create conversion request from one currency to the other.
create-rfq.body:
`Create RFQ`, `Get RFQ`, and `Accept RFQ` example responses all stop at `RFQ_PENDING_REVIEW`. The fields integrators actually need to render a quote — `destinationAmount`, `quotedRate`, `effectiveRate`, `feePercentage`, `quoteExpiresAt` — only appear in the `Get RFQs` list example (because the seed data there happens to include a `TRANSACTION_COMPLETED` record).

*Add a `QUOTE_SENT` example to each of the three single-RFQ endpoints with all quote fields populated.*

get-rfqs.anchor: Retrieve list of all RFQ with pagination
get-rfqs.body:
Two status taxonomies run in parallel: `status: RFQ_*` (internal) and `customerStatus: Quote_*` / `"Transaction completed"` (customer-facing). The split isn't documented.

*Add a mapping table to the RFQ section overview so integrators know which field to render and which to branch on.*

list-virtual-accounts.anchor: Retrieves paginated list of virtual bank accounts for the authenticated partner
list-virtual-accounts.body:
"Virtual Accounts" and "Receive Accounts - Latin America" describe the same concept in two sibling sidebar sections. The split is presumably regulatory (LatAm rails work differently) but the doc never says so.

*Merge under one heading with a regional sub-grouping, or add a "Why two sections?" intro to each.*
